recipes.title: Jar Lantern
recipes.pitch: Pinch an LED onto a coin cell and drop it into a glass jar for a cordless table lantern.
assembly_steps: Spread the LED's legs about 5 mm apart and slide the coin cell between them, + face against the long leg. It should light at once; if not, flip the cell.
Wrap one turn of tape around the legs and cell so they stay pressed together. Leave the cell's edge free so you can slide it out to switch off.
Crumple a sheet of paper loosely into the jar as a diffuser, then nest the LED pod in the middle, facing up.
Cut 60 cm of string, wrap it twice under the jar's rim and knot it, then tie the ends into a carry loop about 15 cm above the lid.
Test it in a dark room. A coin cell runs one LED for about a day; if the light fades within hours, the cell is old, so swap it.
recipes.extend: Add a light sensor and transistor so the lantern turns on by itself at dusk.

recipes.title: Bottle Desk Lamp
recipes.pitch: A USB LED strip coiled inside a plastic bottle makes a soft desk lamp powered from any charger.
assembly_steps: Solder or splice the LED strip to the USB cable: red to 5V, black to ground.
Coil the strip around the inside wall of the bottle and feed the cable out the neck.
Cut a notch in the bottle cap for the cable and screw the cap on as a base plug.
recipes.extend: Spray the bottle with frosted paint or wrap in paper for an even, diffused glow.

recipes.title: Solar Light Revival
recipes.pitch: Bring a dead solar garden light back with a fresh rechargeable cell and give it a jar housing.
assembly_steps: Open the garden light, remove the dead battery, and fit the rechargeable AA in the same direction.
Cover the solar cell for 5 seconds to check the LED turns on.
Mount the solar unit in the jar lid, panel facing up, and hang the jar by string.
recipes.extend: Group three revived jars on one rope for a solar string light.

recipes.title: Auto Night Light
recipes.pitch: A light sensor and transistor switch an LED on when the room goes dark.
assembly_steps: Wire the light sensor and transistor so the sensor pulls the transistor base low in daylight.
Connect the LED to the transistor collector through the battery holder.
Cover your hand over the sensor to test, then place the circuit under an egg carton cup as a shade.
recipes.extend: Add a second LED and a button to pick between warm and cool colors.

recipes.title: Clip-On Book Light
recipes.pitch: An LED pod glued onto a clothespin clips to any book or shelf edge.
assembly_steps: Tape the LED legs around the coin cell so it lights.
Glue the LED pod to the top of the clothespin, pointing forward.
Clip onto a book cover and angle the LED onto the page.
recipes.extend: Add a slide switch between the LED and cell so you stop pulling the battery out.

recipes.title: Tracing Light Box
recipes.pitch: An LED strip under a clear tray turns into a light table for tracing drawings.
assembly_steps: Wire the LED strip to the USB cable, red to 5V and black to ground.
Zigzag the strip across a cardboard base sized to the tray.
Set the clear tray on top, lay paper on the tray, and plug in.
recipes.extend: Tape a sheet of white paper under the tray to remove LED hot spots.

recipes.title: Under-Cabinet Light Bar
recipes.pitch: A USB LED strip on velcro sticks under a shelf and runs off a power bank.
assembly_steps: Wire the LED strip to the USB cable.
Stick the velcro hook side to the strip and the loop side under the cabinet.
Press the bar into place and plug into the power bank.
recipes.extend: Add a motion sensor so the bar turns on when you reach in.

recipes.title: Tin Can Lantern
recipes.pitch: Punch a star pattern into a tin can and throw dots of light across the room.
assembly_steps: Fill the can with water, freeze overnight, then tap a nail through in a pattern.
Thaw and dry the can, then set the LED pod inside.
Bend the hanger into a handle and hook through two holes at the rim.
recipes.extend: Swap the coin cell LED for a solar unit from an old garden light.

recipes.title: Bike Tail Light
recipes.pitch: A red LED, battery holder and switch strapped to the seat post with inner tube rubber. An extra visibility light: use it alongside a proper bike light, not instead of one.
assembly_steps: Wire the LED to the battery holder, adding a resistor if your LED needs one.
Splice the toggle switch into the red battery wire.
Cut a strip of inner tube and stretch it around the seat post to hold the light.
recipes.extend: Add a 555 timer chip so the light blinks instead of staying on.

recipes.title: Shadow Lamp
recipes.pitch: Punch a pattern into a paper towel tube and light it from inside to throw shadows on the wall.
assembly_steps: Poke a pattern of holes along the tube with a nail.
Stand the tube on a cardboard base and drop the LED pod inside.
Turn off the room lights and watch the pattern on the walls.
recipes.extend: Use a ring of three LEDs for brighter, sharper shadows.

recipes.title: Bristlebot
recipes.pitch: A phone vibration motor on a toothbrush head makes a tiny robot buzz across the table.
assembly_steps: Cut the head off the toothbrush, keeping about 1 cm of handle. Angled bristles make it walk; perfectly straight ones make it buzz in place.
Press a strip of double-sided tape along the top of the head.
Touch the vibration motor's two wires to the coin cell's faces and tape one wire down. The free wire is your on switch.
Stick the motor near the front of the head and the cell behind it, keeping the weight low and centered.
Set it on a smooth table and connect the free wire. If it tips over, move the cell lower; if it spins in circles, shift the motor toward the middle.
recipes.extend: Build two and race them inside a cardboard arena.

recipes.title: Scribble Bot
recipes.pitch: An off-balance motor shakes a plastic cup on marker legs into a drawing robot.
assembly_steps: Push a cork slice onto the motor shaft off-center to create a wobble.
Wire the motor to the battery holder.
Tape three markers around an upside-down cup as legs, mount the drive on top, and set it on paper.
recipes.extend: Add a switch and try different cork sizes to change the drawing pattern.

recipes.title: Rubber Band Car
recipes.pitch: Wind a rubber band around the axle and let go to send a cardboard car down the hall.
assembly_steps: Push each dowel through the center of two bottle caps to make axles.
Poke the axles through the sides of the cardboard chassis.
Hook a rubber band to the front of the chassis and wrap the other end around the rear axle, then wind and release.
recipes.extend: Swap bottle caps for CDs to make bigger wheels and a longer run.

recipes.title: Balloon Rocket Car
recipes.pitch: A balloon taped to a straw pushes a plastic bottle car across the floor with air.
assembly_steps: Tape the balloon neck tight around one end of the straw.
Push the axles through holes in the bottle's sides.
Tape the jet on top, blow up the balloon through the straw, pinch, set down, and let go.
recipes.extend: Add a second balloon jet and measure the distance gain.

recipes.title: Solar Car
recipes.pitch: A small solar panel drives a DC motor geared to a cardboard car's back axle.
assembly_steps: Wire the solar panel to the motor and check the shaft spins in sunlight.
Press a gear on the motor shaft so the gear meshes with a gear or rubber band on the rear axle.
Mount the axles and drive on the cardboard chassis and test in full sun.
recipes.extend: Add a small rechargeable cell so the car keeps rolling in shade.

recipes.title: Hydraulic Arm
recipes.pitch: Water-filled syringes push popsicle-stick links, so you move the arm by squeezing a plunger.
assembly_steps: Fill one syringe with water, connect tubing, and push the water into a second syringe to remove air.
Join popsicle sticks with brass fasteners to make three hinged links.
Glue the links to a cardboard base and fix one syringe of each line across a joint.
recipes.extend: Add a third line and a clothespin gripper on the end.

recipes.title: Guarded USB Fan
recipes.pitch: Cut soft vanes from a plastic bottle, put them on a small motor behind a mesh guard, and run it from a USB charger.
assembly_steps: Cut the top 6 cm off a plastic bottle and slice it into 4 vanes from the rim to the neck. Twist each vane slightly the same way.
Glue the bottle cap onto the motor shaft, then glue the bottle top onto the cap so the vanes spin with it.
Wire the motor to the USB cable: red to red, black to black, and tape each joint separately.
Wrap the window mesh around the vanes as a cage and tape it to the motor body, leaving 1 cm of space so nothing rubs.
Stand it on the tin can and plug in. If it wobbles, trim the longest vane; if air blows backward, swap the two motor wires.
recipes.extend: Add a switch and a second speed using a resistor.

recipes.title: Pan-Tilt Mount
recipes.pitch: Two servos on brackets aim a phone camera from an Arduino.
assembly_steps: Screw each servo to an L-bracket.
Stack the tilt mount on top of the pan servo horn.
Wire both servos to the Arduino and run the Sweep example to test.
recipes.extend: Add a joystick or two potentiometers for manual control.

recipes.title: Cardboard Robot Hand
recipes.pitch: Pull strings threaded through straws to curl cardboard fingers, like tendons in a real hand.
assembly_steps: Trace your hand on cardboard, cut it out, and crease each finger at the knuckles.
Cut straws into short pieces and glue them along each finger.
Thread a string through each finger's straws and tie it at the fingertip, then pull.
recipes.extend: Tie the strings to servo horns so an Arduino curls the fingers.

recipes.title: Mini Conveyor
recipes.pitch: An inner tube belt wraps two dowel rollers, and a DC motor drives one end.
assembly_steps: Glue the motor shaft into a hole drilled in one dowel.
Set both rollers across a wooden frame and stretch the inner tube around them.
Wire the motor to the battery holder and adjust roller spacing until the belt tracks straight.
recipes.extend: Add a light sensor at the end to stop the belt when an object arrives.

recipes.title: Self-Watering Planter
recipes.pitch: A 2-liter bottle cut in two, with a T-shirt wick through the cap, pulls water up to the soil so the plant waters itself for days.
assembly_steps: Cut a 2-liter bottle all the way around about 10 cm below the neck. Sand or tape the cut edge so it isn't sharp.
Twist a nail through the center of the cap to make a hole about 5 mm wide, then screw the cap back on the top half.
Cut a T-shirt strip about 3 cm wide and 25 cm long. Wet it and thread half of it up through the cap hole.
Flip the top half into the base like a funnel, so the wick hangs into the base. Fill the base with water to about 3 cm below the cap.
Fill the top half with soil around the wick and plant. Check after a day: if the soil is still dry, re-wet the wick and push it 5 cm deeper into the soil.
recipes.extend: Add a clear window strip so you see the water level.

recipes.title: Bottle Drip Irrigator
recipes.pitch: A bottle with pinholes in the cap drips water slowly into a pot over a day.
assembly_steps: Poke two small holes in the bottle cap with a hot nail.
Fill the bottle, screw on the cap, and cut the bottom off for refills.
Push the bottle neck-down into the soil next to the plant.
recipes.extend: Run tubing from one big bucket to several drip caps.

recipes.title: Auto Plant Waterer
recipes.pitch: A moisture sensor tells an Arduino when to run a USB pump from a water bucket.
assembly_steps: Wire the moisture sensor to the Arduino: VCC to 5V, GND to GND, signal to A0. Push the sensor into dry soil and note the reading, then water and note it again.
Wire the USB pump through the transistor: pump + to 5V, pump - to the transistor's collector, emitter to GND, base to pin 7 through a 1 kOhm resistor.
Push the silicone tubing onto the pump outlet, drop the pump in the bucket of water, and run the tubing into the plant pot.
Upload a sketch that runs the pump for 3 seconds when the reading crosses halfway between your dry and wet numbers, then waits 10 minutes before checking again.
Power everything from the power bank and watch the first cycle. If water siphons after the pump stops, lift the tube's end above the bucket's water line.
recipes.extend: Log moisture readings to the serial monitor and graph a week of data.

recipes.title: Egg Carton Seed Starter
recipes.pitch: An egg carton under plastic wrap acts as a mini greenhouse for seedlings.
assembly_steps: Fill each egg cup with soil and press in a seed.
Set the carton on a tray and stretch plastic wrap over the top.
Mist daily and remove the wrap once sprouts touch it.
recipes.extend: Cut the cups apart and plant them straight into the ground, since the carton breaks down.

recipes.title: Vertical Pallet Garden
recipes.pitch: Pallet planks and fabric pockets turn a wall into an herb garden.
assembly_steps: Screw two planks into a ladder-style frame.
Staple fabric under three more planks to form deep pockets.
Screw the pockets across the frame, fill with soil, and lean against a sunny wall.
recipes.extend: Add the bottle drip irrigator at the top pocket so water trickles down.

recipes.title: Bucket Composter
recipes.pitch: Drill holes in a bucket and lid to make an airflow compost bin for kitchen scraps.
assembly_steps: Punch holes around the bucket sides and bottom with a hot nail.
Set the bucket on a tray to catch drips.
Layer scraps with dry leaves and stir weekly.
recipes.extend: Stack a second bucket inside so finished compost drops out the bottom.

recipes.title: Rain Gauge
recipes.pitch: A straight-sided bottle with a ruler scale measures rainfall.
assembly_steps: Cut the top off the bottle and flip it in as a funnel.
Add gravel to the bottom for weight, add water up to a starting line, and mark centimeters above it.
Set the gauge in an open spot and read it after each rain.
recipes.extend: Log readings and compare with the local weather service.

recipes.title: Bottle Bird Feeder
recipes.pitch: Two dowels through a bottle make perches, and seeds pour out of holes above them.
assembly_steps: Push a dowel through the bottle near the bottom, and cut a small hole above each end.
Fill the bottle with birdseed and close the cap.
Tie string around the neck and hang the feeder from a branch.
recipes.extend: Add an old phone camera to snap visitors.

recipes.title: Bug Hotel
recipes.pitch: A tin can packed with straws and paper tubes gives solitary bees a place to nest.
assembly_steps: Cut straws and paper tubes to the can's depth.
Pack them in tight so none fall out.
Hang the can on its side, opening facing south, out of the rain.
recipes.extend: Mount several cans in a wooden box to make a bug apartment block.

recipes.title: Hose Sprinkler
recipes.pitch: A bottle with nail holes on a hose end makes a lawn sprinkler.
assembly_steps: Poke rows of holes along one side of the bottle.
Push the hose into the bottle neck and wrap with duct tape until watertight.
Lay the bottle holes-up and turn on the water slowly.
recipes.extend: Mount the sprinkler on a servo to sweep the spray.

recipes.title: Cardboard Phone Stand
recipes.pitch: Two interlocking cardboard pieces hold a phone at a viewing angle.
assembly_steps: Cut two cardboard rectangles, 12 x 15 cm each. Cut a slot 7.5 cm deep and as wide as the cardboard's thickness into the middle of each, one from the top and one from the bottom.
Slide the two pieces together at the slots so they form a cross, then tip it so one face leans back about 20 degrees.
Tape every joint on both sides so the cross can't fold flat.
Glue the bottle cap across the front bottom edge as a lip that stops the phone sliding off.
Set your phone on it. If it tips backward, trim 1 cm off the back leg; if the phone slides, add a second cap beside the first.
recipes.extend: Cut a hole at the back to feed a charging cable through.

recipes.title: Desk Cable Clips
recipes.pitch: Binder clips taped to the desk edge keep charging cables from falling behind.
assembly_steps: Tape each binder clip to the back edge of the desk.
Thread a cable through each clip's metal handle.
Label each clip with a strip of tape.
recipes.extend: Add a wooden block to hold the clips and screw it to the desk.

recipes.title: Tin Can Pencil Caddy
recipes.pitch: Three tin cans glued onto a board hold pens, scissors, and rulers.
assembly_steps: Wrap each can in fabric scrap and glue the edge.
Glue the three cans upright onto the wood base, tallest at the back.
Sort pens, scissors, and rulers into each can.
recipes.extend: Add a magnet to the base to hold paper clips.

recipes.title: Headphone Hook
recipes.pitch: A bent hanger clamped under the desk holds headphones.
assembly_steps: Bend the hanger into a J shape about 10 cm deep.
Clamp the flat end under the desk edge with the binder clip.
Wrap the hook in duct tape so it won't scratch the headband.
recipes.extend: Add a second hook for a cable and a small shelf for the case.

recipes.title: Laptop Cooling Pad
recipes.pitch: A PC fan powered by USB pushes air under a laptop on a cardboard stand.
assembly_steps: Splice the fan's red wire to the USB cable's red (5V) and black to black, and tape each joint separately. A 12V fan spins slower on 5V, which is quieter and fine here.
Cut a hole in the cardboard the size of the fan's blade circle, centered where the laptop's air vents sit.
Mount the fan under the hole so the arrow on its housing points up, toward the laptop.
Glue the window mesh over the hole so fingers and cables can't reach the fan.
Fold the cardboard into a wedge about 4 cm tall at the back. Run the laptop for 15 minutes: the underside should feel cooler; if not, check the fan's airflow arrow.
recipes.extend: Add a second fan and a switch.

recipes.title: Magnetic Key Holder
recipes.pitch: Magnets glued into a plank hold keys by the door.
assembly_steps: Glue a magnet into a shallow hole at the center of the wood.
Screw two hooks into the wood bottom for keys with plastic heads.
Mount the holder by the door with screws.
recipes.extend: Add an LED that turns on when keys are missing, using a reed switch.

recipes.title: Drawer Dividers
recipes.pitch: Paper towel tubes cut to height sort cables and small items in a drawer.
assembly_steps: Cut tubes to the drawer's height.
Tape them together in a grid inside a shoe box.
Slide the box into the drawer and roll cables into each tube.
recipes.extend: Label each tube by cable type.

recipes.title: Floating Plank Shelf
recipes.pitch: A pallet plank on two L-brackets makes a sturdy wall shelf.
assembly_steps: Sand the plank smooth, edges and face.
Screw the brackets into wall studs at the same height.
Set the plank on top and screw up through the brackets.
recipes.extend: Add an LED strip under the shelf for a display light.

recipes.title: Denim Doorstop
recipes.pitch: A jeans leg filled with dry rice holds a door open.
assembly_steps: Cut a 20 cm length of jean leg.
Zip-tie one end, fill with rice, then zip-tie the other end.
Fold the ends under and push against the door.
recipes.extend: Sew a fabric handle on top for carrying.

recipes.title: Cork Coasters
recipes.pitch: Wine cork slices glued into a circle make coasters.
assembly_steps: Slice corks into 1 cm rounds.
Glue the rounds tight on a cardboard circle.
Trim the edge and seal with clear glue.
recipes.extend: Burn designs into the cork with a hot nail.

recipes.title: Jar Lid Spice Rack
recipes.pitch: Jar lids screwed under a shelf let spice jars hang and twist off.
assembly_steps: Screw each lid to the plank bottom.
Fill the jars and twist them into the lids.
Mount the plank under a cabinet.
recipes.extend: Label lids with marker so you know the contents from below.

recipes.title: Bag Dispenser
recipes.pitch: A cut bottle on the wall stores plastic bags and dispenses them one at a time.
assembly_steps: Cut the bottom off the bottle.
Screw the bottle neck-down to a wall.
Stuff bags in the top and pull them from the neck.
recipes.extend: Wrap the bottle in fabric to match the room.

recipes.title: PVC Shoe Rack
recipes.pitch: PVC pipe sections stacked in a pyramid hold one shoe pair per tube.
assembly_steps: Cut pipe into 30 cm lengths.
Zip-tie pipes into pairs and stack them into a pyramid.
Glue the pyramid onto a wooden base.
recipes.extend: Spray-paint the pipes and add a top shelf.

recipes.title: PVC Tool Wall
recipes.pitch: Short PVC sleeves screwed to a plank hold screwdrivers and pliers on a wall.
assembly_steps: Cut the PVC pipe into five 5 cm sleeves and sand the cut edges smooth.
Screw an L-bracket to each end of the plank's back, so it stands off the wall.
Lay the sleeves along the plank 6 cm apart, openings up, and screw each one on through its back with one screw.
Find a wall stud or use wall plugs, then screw the brackets to the wall with the plank level.
Drop a screwdriver into each sleeve. If tools tip forward, angle the sleeves back slightly or switch to a narrower pipe.
recipes.extend: Add a magnet strip along the top for drill bits.

recipes.title: Cable Box
recipes.pitch: A shoe box with side holes hides a power strip and its cable mess.
assembly_steps: Cut a slot in each end of the box for cables.
Punch vent holes in the lid.
Set the power strip inside, route cables out the slots, and tape the edges.
recipes.extend: Cover with fabric for a cleaner look.

recipes.title: No-Sew T-Shirt Bag
recipes.pitch: Cut and knot an old T-shirt into a strong shopping bag.
assembly_steps: Cut off the sleeves and widen the neck to make handles.
Cut 8 cm fringe along the bottom hem.
Tie each front fringe to its back pair, then tie neighbors together.
recipes.extend: Line the bag with a second shirt for heavier loads.

recipes.title: Cereal Box File
recipes.pitch: A cereal box cut at an angle holds magazines and notebooks.
assembly_steps: Cut the cereal box diagonally from top back to halfway down the front.
Glue fabric over the outside.
Line two files on a shelf.
recipes.extend: Add a label pocket on the front.

recipes.title: Under-Bed Roller Box
recipes.pitch: Caster wheels under a shallow wooden box let you roll storage under the bed.
assembly_steps: Screw scrap wood into a 15 cm deep box.
Screw a caster on each corner.
Add a rope handle at one end.
recipes.extend: Add a hinged lid to keep dust out.

recipes.title: Jeans Pocket Organizer
recipes.pitch: Back pockets cut from old jeans and stapled to a plank hold small items.
assembly_steps: Cut the back pockets off the jeans, leaving 2 cm of fabric around each one.
Staple the pockets in a grid onto the plank, open side up.
Screw two hooks into the top edge and hang the board by the door.
recipes.extend: Add a mirror in the center for an entryway station.

recipes.title: Hardware Jar Wall
recipes.pitch: Clear jars sorted on a shelf with labeled lids show every screw size.
assembly_steps: Write a size on each lid with marker.
Fill each jar with one fastener type.
Mount the plank on brackets and line up the jars.
recipes.extend: Glue a sample of each fastener on the lid.

recipes.title: Passive Phone Amp
recipes.pitch: A paper towel tube between two cups makes your phone louder without power.
assembly_steps: Cut a phone-width slot in the center of the tube.
Cut a hole in each cup side and push the tube ends in.
Glue to a cardboard base and drop the phone in the slot.
recipes.extend: Swap cups for a bigger cone to boost volume.

recipes.title: Bluetooth Speaker Revival
recipes.pitch: A Bluetooth audio module and amp board give an old speaker a second life.
assembly_steps: Check the speaker's label: the amp board needs a 4 or 8 ohm speaker. A speaker outside that range can overheat the board.
Wire the Bluetooth module's left output and ground to the amp board's input, keeping the wires short.
Wire the amp's output + and - to the speaker's + and - tabs. Reversed polarity still plays, but bass sounds thin.
Cut a hole in the shoe box the size of the speaker cone and glue the speaker in from inside. Pack crumpled paper around it to stop rattles.
Power it from the power bank, pair your phone, and start at low volume. If it crackles, the amp is clipping, so lower the phone's volume.
recipes.extend: Add a second speaker for stereo.

recipes.title: Tin Can Telephone
recipes.pitch: Two cans on a tight string carry your voice across the yard.
assembly_steps: Punch a small hole in each can bottom.
Thread the string through and knot it inside.
Pull the string tight and talk into one can.
recipes.extend: Branch a third can on the line for a party line.

recipes.title: Rubber Band Guitar
recipes.pitch: Rubber bands stretched over a shoe box sound different pitches.
assembly_steps: Cut a round hole in the shoe box lid.
Stretch rubber bands of different widths across the hole.
Glue a tube on as a neck and pluck.
recipes.extend: Add a pencil bridge under the bands to tune.

recipes.title: Bottle Xylophone
recipes.pitch: Bottles filled to different levels ring out a scale.
assembly_steps: Mark a fill line on each bottle, a little higher on each one.
Fill each bottle with water to its line and line them up.
Tap with a dowel and adjust levels until you hear a scale.
recipes.extend: Add food coloring per note and write a song chart.

recipes.title: Buzzer Doorbell
recipes.pitch: A push button and piezo buzzer make a battery doorbell.
assembly_steps: Cut two lengths of hookup wire long enough to reach from the door to where you'll hear the bell.
Wire the push button in series with the buzzer: battery + to button, button to buzzer +, buzzer - to battery -.
Press the button to test before mounting. A piezo buzzer only sounds one way round, so swap its wires if it's silent.
Tape the button beside the door frame and run the wire along the frame to the buzzer and battery holder inside.
Ring it from outside with the door closed. If it's too quiet, mount the buzzer on a hard surface like a cupboard door to amplify it.
recipes.extend: Use an Arduino to play a tune instead of a beep.

recipes.title: Bucket Drum
recipes.pitch: A balloon stretched over a bucket makes a deep drum.
assembly_steps: Cut the neck off a balloon.
Stretch the balloon over the bucket rim and tape the edge.
Play with two dowel sticks.
recipes.extend: Add bottle caps on a wire as a jingle.

recipes.title: Tube Kazoo
recipes.pitch: Wax paper over a tube buzzes when you hum.
assembly_steps: Cover one end of the tube with wax paper.
Hold the paper with a rubber band.
Poke a small hole in the side and hum into the open end.
recipes.extend: Make three kazoos of different lengths and compare pitch.

recipes.title: Key Wind Chimes
recipes.pitch: Old keys and spoons on strings ring against each other in the wind.
assembly_steps: Tie keys and spoons to strings at different lengths.
Bend the hanger into a ring.
Tie the strands around the ring and hang in a breezy spot.
recipes.extend: Add a center clapper on a long string.

recipes.title: Keyboard Piano
recipes.pitch: Old keyboard keys wired to an Arduino and buzzer play notes.
assembly_steps: Pull the key matrix from the old keyboard and find rows and columns.
Wire the matrix to the Arduino inputs and the buzzer to a PWM pin.
Upload a sketch mapping 8 keys to a scale.
recipes.extend: Add a record button to save and replay melodies.

recipes.title: Marble Run
recipes.pitch: Paper tubes taped to a wall form a run for marbles.
assembly_steps: Tape a large cardboard sheet to a wall or the side of a bookshelf as the backboard.
Cut each paper towel tube in half lengthwise to make open chutes about 25 cm long.
Tape the first chute at the top tilted about 10 degrees, so a marble rolls but doesn't fly off.
Add each next chute in a zigzag, with its high end 3 cm below and overlapping the end of the one above.
Run a marble from the top. If it jumps out at a turn, lower that chute's angle or tape a cardboard wall on the outside of the turn.
recipes.extend: Add a funnel cup and a bell at the end.

recipes.title: Cardboard Pinball
recipes.pitch: A shoe box lid with popsicle stick flippers and a rubber band plunger.
assembly_steps: Prop the shoe box lid at a slight slant with the low end toward you.
Pin two popsicle stick flippers near the bottom with brass fasteners so they swing.
Build a rubber band plunger down the right side, drop in the marble, and pull the plunger to send it up the table.
recipes.extend: Add a buzzer and contacts to score hits.

recipes.title: CD Spinning Top
recipes.pitch: An old CD with a bottle cap handle and a marble tip spins for a long time on a table.
assembly_steps: Glue the bottle cap open side down onto the CD's center hole as a handle.
Glue the marble into the center hole on the other side, so about half of it sticks out as the tip.
Let the glue set for 10 minutes before spinning, or the marble pops out.
Twist the cap between thumb and finger and drop the top flat onto a smooth table.
If it wobbles and falls quickly, the marble is off-center, so re-glue it right in the middle of the hole.
recipes.extend: Draw spirals on the CD with markers and watch the patterns change as it slows.

recipes.title: Kaleidoscope
recipes.pitch: Three mirror strips inside a tube make repeating patterns.
assembly_steps: Cut the mirror into three equal strips and tape them into a triangle, mirror side in.
Slide the triangle into the paper towel tube.
Cover one end with plastic wrap holding a few beads, cap the other end with a bottle cap with a peephole, and turn the tube.
recipes.extend: Make the bead end rotate.

recipes.title: Periscope
recipes.pitch: Two mirrors at 45 degrees in a milk carton see over walls.
assembly_steps: Use a 1-liter milk carton, washed and dried. Cut a 6 x 6 cm window near the top on one side and another near the bottom on the opposite side.
Glue the first mirror inside behind the top window at 45 degrees, facing down. A folded paper triangle makes a good 45-degree guide.
Glue the second mirror behind the bottom window at 45 degrees, facing up, parallel to the first.
Tape the carton closed and cover any light leaks with tape.
Look through the bottom window at something above a wall. If you see the carton's inside, one mirror's angle is off, so reset it with the paper guide.
recipes.extend: Join two cartons for a taller scope.

recipes.title: Bottle Shaker
recipes.pitch: A plastic bottle part-filled with dry rice and taped shut makes a rhythm shaker.
assembly_steps: Use a small, dry plastic bottle. Pour in dry rice until it's about a quarter full.
Shake it to test the sound: more rice gives a softer swish, less gives a sharper rattle.
Screw the cap on tightly, then wrap duct tape over the cap and down the neck to seal it.
For little kids, add a second layer of tape. Loose rice is a choking hazard.
Play along to a song. If the cap loosens, re-tape it before handing it back.
recipes.extend: Make three with rice, sand and gravel and compare how each sounds.

recipes.title: Tilt Maze
recipes.pitch: Cardboard walls in a box lid guide a marble through a maze.
assembly_steps: Draw a maze path inside the shoe box lid.
Glue cardboard strips on edge along every line to form walls.
Set the marble at the start and tilt the lid to roll it to the finish.
recipes.extend: Cut holes as traps.

recipes.title: Bottle Bowling
recipes.pitch: Ten bottles weighted with sand and a tennis ball.
assembly_steps: Pour two cups of sand into each bottle so the pins stand steady.
Set the ten bottles in a triangle: four, three, two, one.
Roll the tennis ball from three meters back and count the pins knocked down.
recipes.extend: Paint numbers for scoring.

recipes.title: Ring Toss
recipes.pitch: Hose rings toss onto bottle targets.
assembly_steps: Cut the hose into 40 cm lengths and tape each into a ring.
Pour sand into the bottles and stand them a step apart.
Mark a throwing line two meters back and toss the rings onto the bottle necks.
recipes.extend: Assign point values.

recipes.title: Puppet Theater
recipes.pitch: A box with a cut stage window and sock puppets.
assembly_steps: Cut a large window in the bottom of the shoe box and stand the box on its side.
Glue fabric curtains along the top edge of the window.
Glue felt eyes and a mouth onto each sock and perform from behind the box.
recipes.extend: Add an LED spotlight.

recipes.title: Solar Phone Charger
recipes.pitch: A small solar panel and a USB charge module top up a power bank on a hike or at camp.
assembly_steps: Check the panel's label for its voltage. The USB charge module needs about 5 to 6V in; a 6V panel is ideal.
Wire the panel's + and - to the module's IN+ and IN-. Reversed wires won't charge, so check polarity twice.
Plug the power bank into the module's USB output.
Prop the panel facing the sun at roughly your latitude's angle, for example 35 to 40 degrees in most of the US.
Check that the power bank shows charging. A small 1W panel charges slowly, so expect hours for a full charge; clouds cut output sharply.
recipes.extend: Add a folding cardboard stand that angles the panel toward the sun.

recipes.title: Tarp Shelter
recipes.pitch: An old tarp over a rope ridgeline makes a quick rain shelter between two trees.
assembly_steps: Tie a rope tight between two trees at chest height.
Drape the tarp over the rope so both sides hang evenly.
Tie a rope to each lower corner and stake them out to pull the walls taut.
recipes.extend: Add a third tarp panel as a floor to keep gear dry.

recipes.title: Camp Lantern
recipes.pitch: A USB LED strip coiled in a jar runs for hours off a power bank.
assembly_steps: Wire the LED strip to the USB cable.
Coil the strip inside the jar and feed the cable out a notch in the lid.
Bend the hanger into a handle around the jar neck.
recipes.extend: Add a red LED mode so you keep your night vision.

recipes.title: Paper Plate Sundial
recipes.pitch: A dowel through a paper plate casts a shadow you mark hour by hour.
assembly_steps: Push the dowel through the plate center and stand the plate flat in a sunny spot.
At each hour, mark where the shadow falls and write the hour.
Leave the plate in place and read the time the next day.
recipes.extend: Rebuild the sundial on a wood base with the dowel tilted to your latitude.

recipes.title: Bike Phone Mount
recipes.pitch: Inner tube bands and zip ties hold a phone on the handlebars.
assembly_steps: Cut four 2 cm bands from the inner tube.
Zip-tie a sponge pad to the handlebar as a cushion.
Set the phone on the pad and stretch the bands over each corner.
recipes.extend: Add a USB cable run to a power bank in a frame bag.

recipes.title: Water Clarifier Demo
recipes.pitch: Layers of cloth, sand, and gravel in a bottle clear muddy water. For demonstration only, not for drinking.
assembly_steps: Cut the bottom off the bottle and set the bottle neck-down over a cup.
Stuff a T-shirt scrap in the neck, then add sand, then gravel.
Pour muddy water in the top and compare the result to the start.
recipes.extend: Add a charcoal layer and test the difference in clarity.

recipes.title: Bag Kite
recipes.pitch: A plastic bag stretched over two crossed dowels flies in light wind.
assembly_steps: Cross a 60 cm dowel and a 50 cm dowel, with the shorter one a quarter of the way down the longer, and tie the cross tightly with string.
Cut a plastic bag open into a flat sheet. Lay the cross on it and cut a diamond 2 cm larger than the frame on every side.
Fold the extra 2 cm over the dowel ends and tape it down at all four tips.
Tie a 40 cm bridle string from the cross to the bottom tip, then tie the flying line to the bridle about a third of the way down.
Tape a 2 m tail of bag strips to the bottom tip. If the kite spins or dives, add tail length; if it won't climb, move the line's knot up.
recipes.extend: Add a tail of bag strips for stability in gusty wind.

recipes.title: Outdoor Thermometer
recipes.pitch: A temperature sensor on an Arduino reports outdoor readings from inside a vented bottle.
assembly_steps: Wire the sensor to the Arduino and run the sensor library example.
Cut vent slots in the bottle and mount the sensor inside, out of direct sun.
Power from the battery holder and print readings to the serial monitor.
recipes.extend: Add a small screen so you read the temperature without a laptop.

recipes.title: Plank Birdhouse
recipes.pitch: Pallet planks nailed into a box with a hinged side you open for cleaning.
assembly_steps: Cut planks for a floor, four walls, and a sloped roof, with a 3 cm hole in the front.
Nail the floor, back, front, and roof together.
Hinge the last side so it opens, then hang from the hook.
recipes.extend: Add an old phone or camera inside to watch the nest.

recipes.title: Elastic Headlamp
recipes.pitch: An LED pod in a bottle cap reflector on an elastic band.
assembly_steps: Tape the LED to the coin cell so it lights.
Line a bottle cap with foil and glue the LED pod inside as a reflector.
Glue or sew the cap to the elastic band and fit to your head.
recipes.extend: Add a switch so you turn it off without removing the battery.

recipes.title: Magnetic Parts Tray
recipes.pitch: A magnet glued under a tray holds screws while you work.
assembly_steps: Glue the magnet to the center of the tray bottom.
Let the glue cure overnight.
Drop screws in and flip the tray to check they hold.
recipes.extend: Add a second magnet so the tray sticks to the side of a toolbox.

recipes.title: Sanding Block
recipes.pitch: Sandpaper wrapped around a wood block for flat, even sanding.
assembly_steps: Cut a block that fits your hand.
Wrap sandpaper around the bottom and sides.
Clamp the ends with binder clips so you swap paper fast.
recipes.extend: Glue a sponge layer under the paper for curved surfaces.

recipes.title: Cord Reel
recipes.pitch: A dowel through a wood frame winds extension cords without tangles.
assembly_steps: Cut two wood ends and drill a hole in each.
Slide the dowel through both and screw on a crank handle.
Wind the cord around the dowel.
recipes.extend: Mount the reel on the wall with a bracket.

recipes.title: Jar Lid Screw Sorter
recipes.pitch: Jar lids screwed under a shelf hold jars of screws, nails, and bolts.
assembly_steps: Screw each lid to the plank bottom.
Fill jars by size and twist them into the lids.
Mount the plank above the bench.
recipes.extend: Add a label on each lid and a magnet strip for loose bits.

recipes.title: Helping Hands
recipes.pitch: Alligator clips on bent hanger arms hold small parts for soldering.
assembly_steps: Bend two hanger arms with a loop at one end.
Fix an alligator clip on each loop with tape.
Fill the can with rice for weight and push the arms in.
recipes.extend: Add a magnifying lens arm.

recipes.title: Bench Hook
recipes.pitch: A board with two cleats holds wood steady for sawing.
assembly_steps: Screw a strip under one end of the board.
Screw a strip on top at the opposite end.
Sand edges and hook over the bench edge.
recipes.extend: Add a 45 degree guide for miter cuts.

recipes.title: Tool Tote
recipes.pitch: Wood sides and a dowel handle make an open carry box for tools.
assembly_steps: Screw scrap wood into an open box.
Cut two tall end pieces with holes near the top.
Slide the dowel through as a handle and screw it in place.
recipes.extend: Add a divider down the middle.

recipes.title: Clamp Rack
recipes.pitch: A plank with spaced dowels holds clamps on the wall.
assembly_steps: Drill angled holes along the plank.
Glue dowel pegs in each hole.
Screw the plank to the wall.
recipes.extend: Add labels for each clamp size.

recipes.title: Shop Dust Bin
recipes.pitch: A bucket with a mesh screen catches sawdust from sanding.
assembly_steps: Cut mesh to fit over the bucket.
Tape mesh across the top.
Sand over the bucket and empty weekly.
recipes.extend: Add a PC fan below to pull dust down.

recipes.title: Magnet Stud Finder
recipes.pitch: A magnet on string finds the screws inside drywall that mark studs.
assembly_steps: Tie the magnet to string.
Drag slowly across the wall.
Mark where the magnet sticks with tape.
recipes.extend: Mount the magnet in a cork so it slides smooth.

recipes.title: Electromagnet
recipes.pitch: Coil wire around a nail and connect a battery to pick up paper clips.
assembly_steps: Use insulated or enamelled wire. Leave 15 cm free at one end, then wrap 50 tight turns along the nail in one direction only.
Strip or sand 1 cm of insulation off both wire ends.
Touch the ends to the battery holder's + and - for a few seconds at a time. The coil and battery get warm, so never leave it connected.
Hold the nail tip near a pile of paper clips and count how many it lifts.
Unwind to 25 turns and count again. Fewer turns lifts fewer clips; if it lifts none, check that the wire ends are bare.
recipes.extend: Add a switch and compare wraps.

recipes.title: Potato Battery
recipes.pitch: Copper and zinc in potatoes power an LED.
assembly_steps: Push a copper coin and a galvanized nail into each potato about 3 cm apart. Don't let them touch inside.
Wire the coin of potato one to the nail of potato two, and the coin of potato two to the nail of potato three.
You now have about 2.4V total: each cell gives roughly 0.8V. Two cells are rarely enough for an LED.
Connect the LED's long leg to the free coin and its short leg to the free nail. Look closely in a dim room: the glow is faint.
If it doesn't light, flip the LED. Still nothing: add a fourth potato in the chain or push the metals deeper.
recipes.extend: Measure voltage per cell.

recipes.title: Cup Anemometer
recipes.pitch: Four cups on straws spin to measure wind speed.
assembly_steps: Tape a cup on the end of each straw, all cups facing the same way around.
Cross the straws in pairs and pin the center to the top of the dowel with a brass fastener.
Stand the dowel outside and count spins in one minute to compare wind speeds.
recipes.extend: Add a magnet and sensor to count automatically.

recipes.title: CD Spectroscope
recipes.pitch: A slice of old CD in a tube splits light into a rainbow.
assembly_steps: Cover one end of the tube with tape, leaving a 1 mm slit.
Tape a piece of CD at a 45 degree angle over the other end, shiny side in.
Point the slit at a light and look at the CD to see the spectrum.
recipes.extend: Compare LED and bulb spectra.

recipes.title: Pizza Box Solar Oven
recipes.pitch: Foil and plastic wrap trap sunlight to melt chocolate.
assembly_steps: Cut a three-sided flap in the pizza box lid and line the flap's underside with foil.
Tape plastic wrap over the opening to seal the window.
Prop the flap with a dowel so it reflects sun into the box, then set chocolate inside.
recipes.extend: Add a thermometer and log temperature.

recipes.title: Pinhole Viewer
recipes.pitch: A shoe box with a foil pinhole projects an upside-down image.
assembly_steps: Cut a 2 cm square hole in one end of the shoe box and tape foil over it.
Poke a clean pinhole in the foil with the tip of a nail.
Tape wax paper inside the far end as a screen, point the pinhole at a bright scene, and look at the screen.
recipes.extend: Use it to view a solar eclipse safely.

recipes.title: Homopolar Motor
recipes.pitch: A battery, magnet, and bent wire spin with no other parts.
assembly_steps: Stand the alkaline AA battery, minus end down, on top of the round magnet.
Bend the bare wire into a loop that touches the top of the battery and the side of the magnet.
Let the loop spin for a few seconds at a time, since the wire and battery get hot.
recipes.extend: Try different wire shapes.

recipes.title: Shoe Box Seismograph
recipes.pitch: A hanging marker draws vibrations on a moving paper strip.
assembly_steps: Hang the marker from the top of the shoe box on a string so the tip just touches the bottom.
Tie a steel washer above the marker as a weight to keep it still.
Slide a paper strip slowly under the tip while someone shakes the table.
recipes.extend: Add vibration sensor.

recipes.title: Jar Barometer
recipes.pitch: A balloon over a jar with a straw needle shows pressure changes.
assembly_steps: Stretch the cut balloon over the jar mouth and seal the edge with a rubber band or tape.
Tape a straw flat on the balloon center so it sticks out past the jar like a needle.
Stand cardboard behind the straw, mark where the needle points, and check the mark each day.
recipes.extend: Log readings twice a day.

recipes.title: Water Compass
recipes.pitch: A magnetized paper clip on cork floats and points north.
assembly_steps: Stroke the paper clip with the magnet 30 times in the same direction.
Lay the magnetized clip flat on a thin cork slice.
Float the cork in a cup of water and watch the clip turn to point north.
recipes.extend: Compare with a phone compass.
